html:
Epicurus was a Greek philosopher who lived from 341 to 270 BCE and founded the school called Epicureanism. He taught that the aim of life is happiness, which he understood as a calm mind and a body free from pain.

He was born on the island of Samos to an Athenian family. He taught first in Mytilene and Lampsacus, then around 306 BCE bought a house and garden in Athens. His school, the Garden, welcomed women and slaves, rare for the time.

His ideas, in brief:

  • Everything is made of atoms moving in the void, as Democritus had taught; see atomism.
  • The gods exist but take no interest in us, so we need not fear them.
  • Death is simply the end of feeling, so "death is nothing to us".
  • Simple pleasures, friendship and a quiet life away from politics bring the most lasting happiness.

He wrote a great deal, but only three letters and some short sayings survive whole, mostly through Diogenes Laertius. The Roman poet Lucretius set his teaching out in verse in On the Nature of Things. His chief rivals were the Stoics.
